 Steve Rifkind Demands Chris Rock Apologize To Loud Records
 Steve Rifkind calls out Chris Rock over his Wu-Tang induction speech and asks for an apology to Loud Records’ staff.
 Nolan Strong • Nov 16, 2026 @ 11:00 AM 
 Add as a preferred source on Google 
 Chris Rock - InstarImages 
 Steve Rifkind wants Chris Rock to apologize to Loud Records’ staff over the comedian’s description of Wu-Tang Clan’s rise during the group’s Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction.
 “Wu-Tang rewrote the rules of hip-hop and did it without a big machine behind them,” Rock said while introducing the group.
 Rifkind answered in the caption of a November 14 Instagram reel : “you owe the staff of Loud apology for what you said.” He also thanked Rock for his compliments about Wu-Tang.
 The executive claimed Rock had previously wanted to release comedy albums through Loud because he admired its work with Wu-Tang and Mobb Deep.
 View this post on Instagram 
 Loud released Wu-Tang’s 1993 debut, “Enter the Wu-Tang (36 Chambers).” Its roster also included Mobb Deep, whose 1995 album “The Infamous” featured “Shook Ones Pt. II.” Rifkind built the label with Rich Isaacson.
 Loud had 30 staff members and RCA/BMG distribution when Rifkind spoke to Music Connection in April 1994 about artist development and grassroots marketing. “I don’t expect to compete with the majors, I expect to beat them,” he said.
 Rifkind has described the work behind those signings in earlier interviews. In a 2020 conversation, he recalled hearing “Protect Ya Neck” on a tape supplied by a member of his college-radio promotions team.
 He said RZA later brought the group to an RCA office in New York, where the rappers performed the record in a cramped room. Rifkind recalled deciding to sign them during that visit.
 RZA speaks on the red carpet at the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction. 
 In the same interview, he pointed to Mobb Deep’s “The Infamous” and Raekwon’s “Only Built 4 Cuban Linx…” as major releases for Loud in 1995. The label also worked with Xzibit and Tha Alkaholiks.
 He also recalled building Loud’s New York A&R team at that time, hiring Schott Free, who brought in Matty C. Rifkind praised their work together developing artists.
 Loud’s Mobb Deep catalog continued with “Hell on Earth” in 1996, “Murda Muzik” in 1999 and “Infamy” in 2001. The duo later left the label and released projects through other companies.
 Rock also spent studio time with Method Man during work on “Tical 2000: Judgement Day.” In a July 2024 Vanity Fair interview , Method Man recalled Rock being present when Janet Jackson recorded the album shout-out he had requested.
 Rifkind’s relationship with the Wu-Tang circle has continued onstage. RZA brought him out during the group’s July 2025 Madison Square Garden concert, where Havoc also performed alongside Raekwon and Ghostface Killah.
 Later that year, LOUD Live and Live Nation announced a joint Raekwon and Mobb Deep tour celebrating the two albums’ 30th anniversaries.
 The announced run covered 19 cities.
